name: Meadow vetchling
grown_as: A native wild flower of meadows, verges and hedge banks, perennial
habit: A scrambling perennial 30 cm to 1 m, leaning on grass and other plants. Stems angled (four-cornered) but not winged, slightly hairy. Spreads by creeping roots; dies down in winter.

leaf.type: Compound: a single pair of leaflets on a short stalk ending in a tendril (simple or branched)
leaf.outline: Each leaflet narrow lance-shaped, 1 to 3 cm by 2 to 8 mm
leaf.veins: Three to five parallel veins running lengthways
leaf.stalk: Short; at its base a pair of large leaf-like stipules shaped like arrowheads, 1 to 2.5 cm, nearly as big as the leaflets

flower.form: Pea flowers in a loose spike
flower.colour: Clear yellow, the standard with faint darker lines
flower.behind: A small green calyx with five teeth
flower.carried: 4 to 12 flowers in a loose spike at the end of a long stalk from the leaf joint, the stalk longer than the leaf, so the flowers stand clear

fruit: Flat pods 2.5 to 3.5 cm, slightly downy, green turning black when ripe, twisting open to scatter small brown seeds
seedling: The seed leaves stay underground. First leaves have one pair of narrow leaflets and a short tendril.
winter: Dies back to the roots; nothing green

leaf: one pair of narrow pointed leaflets
a pair of big arrowhead-shaped stipules at the base
bloom: a loose head of 4 to 12 yellow pea flowers
on a long stalk, longer than the leaf
seedling: a thin shoot with one pair of narrow leaflets
young: a scrambling angled stem with paired narrow leaflets
big arrowhead stipules at each joint
flower: yellow flower heads on long stalks
held above a tangle of grass and leaves

look_alikes: Common bird's-foot-trefoil also has yellow pea flowers but five small leaflets, no tendrils and pods spread like a bird's foot. Yellow vetchling (Lathyrus aphaca) is a rare annual with no leaflets, just huge stipules and single flowers.
